extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and applied empirical social scientists (economists, political scientists) conducting impact evaluations of education policy
extracted.subtask_short: empirical impact evaluation of education policy
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and reporting a district- and village-level empirical impact evaluation of a public school construction program (INPRES) using difference-in-differences, synthetic DID, and robust panel estimators, with cohort and curriculum analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: INPRES intensity definition
rubrics_metrics.description: INPRES intensity is defined as the number of SD INPRES schools constructed from 1973–78 per 1,000 children in 1971.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this normalized measure (per 1,000 children in 1971) as the continuous treatment variable in district-level analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable measurement (district-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dependent variable measures the total number of Islamic schools (or specific subtypes) established by semi-decade and by district per 1,000 children in 1971.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting district-level results present outcomes as new schools per district–year normalized by the 1971 child population (per 1,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable measurement (village-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dependent variable measures the total number of Islamic schools (or specific subtypes) established per village–year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report village-level new-school counts (or indicators for any entry) per village–year and use village fixed-effects specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference-in-differences controls (district)
rubrics_metrics.description: All specifications include district fixed effects and year fixed effects interacted with the 1971 children population, the 1971 enrollment rate, exposure to the water and sanitation program, the number of elementary, junior secondary, senior secondary madrasa in 1959, and the number of pesantren in 1959.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these interactions to account for heterogeneous time trends related to baseline population, enrollment, program exposure, and baseline Islamic-school stocks that informed the policy targeting rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village-level specification controls
rubrics_metrics.description: All village specifications include village fixed effects and year fixed effects interacted with the number of secular elementary schools and Islamic schools in the village as of 1959.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these interactions to allow village-specific time trends conditional on baseline schooling composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Synthetic Difference-in-Differences (SDID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the SDID estimator (Arkhangelsky et al. 2021) to estimate effects; figures report SDID estimates of the effect of SD INPRES on Islamic school entry at the district–year level from 1960–99.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing SDID show trends for treated (above 51st percentile) and weighted comparison groups, display pre-period weights, and indicate the counterfactual parallel trend (dashed diagonal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Residualization before SDID
rubrics_metrics.description: Following Arkhangelsky et al. (2021), apply the SDID estimator to the residuals from equation (1): y_res = y_it − (X'_j θ_t), where X'_j θ_t includes year fixed effects interacted with baseline covariates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residualize outcomes by regressing out the same covariates used in the main DID specification before applying SDID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust DID estimator (Borusyak et al. 2024)
rubrics_metrics.description: For village-level analyses use the robust and efficient estimator from Borusyak et al. (2024) to estimate γ in equation (2) on a balanced panel of villages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report estimates from both standard DID and the robust imputation method to assess sensitivity to missingness/imbalanced panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inference: clustering and cluster bootstrap
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard errors clustered by district in district-level analyses and clustered by village in village-level analyses. For SDID inference use the cluster bootstrap described in Algorithm 2 of Arkhangelsky et al. (2021).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clustering level clearly and use cluster-robust or cluster-bootstrap procedures appropriate to the estimator (e.g., cluster bootstrap for SDID).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report confidence intervals and significance conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures report period-specific β as dots and bars corresponding to 90% confidence intervals; tables use significance stars (* p<0.1, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both point estimates and 90% (or other) confidence intervals graphically, and include conventional significance notation in tables with robust clustered SEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced panel and sample period
rubrics_metrics.description: District–year analyses are estimated on a panel spanning 1960–99 (balanced at the district–year level in the SDID figures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a long panel that covers pre- and post-treatment periods; explicitly state sample years and whether the panel is balanced for the main estimators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of SD INPRES Entry indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: SD INPRES Entry is a binary indicator equal to one in the first year of public primary school construction from 1973–78 and remains one in all years thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this event indicator for village-level event-study and post-entry average effect estimations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort exposure definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohorts: fully-exposed born 1968–1972, partially-exposed born 1963–1967, and unexposed born 1957–1962; cohorts born before 1963 would have fully completed primary schooling before SD INPRES rollout; cohorts from 1968 onward would have been fully exposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define exposure windows clearly for cohort-based analyses of schooling outcomes and present age-specific (birth-year) estimates with a reference cohort (e.g., 1962).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum measurement and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the SIAP registry (2018–19) to measure shares of weekly instruction time devoted to Islamic subjects, Arabic, Pancasila/civic, and Bahasa Indonesia at the school–grade × district × year level; estimating equation includes district fixed effects, grade-level fixed effects, year-of-entry fixed effects, and post-1972 dummy interacted with baseline controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorize subject material consistently (procedure detailed in appendix), and restrict analysis to school–grade × district × year observations where entry occurs; report means and standard deviations for dependent variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of funding potential proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Rice yields: time-invariant standardized measure from FAO-GAEZ (average of dry and wet yields); waqf endowments: data on land endowed in mosques as of 1960. Construct dummy =1 if value is above sample median.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use time-invariant geographic or institutional proxies for local funding potential and interact SD INPRES entry with these dummies to test heterogeneous financing effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy-targeting control set (Table 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: All regressions control for the variables that informed the policy rule for INPRES school allocations: province fixed effects, the 1971 children population, the 1971 enrollment rate, and exposure to the water and sanitation program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing correlates of allocation, include the exact variables used by the policy rule to avoid confounding between policy targeting and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome definitions as shares/fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: For some analyses the dependent variable measures school types as shares of all school entry (e.g., madrasa as share of all formal schools; pesantren and madrasa diniyah as share of all schools including formal and informal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When interpreting composition effects, present outcomes normalized as fractions of total school entry to show relative changes in formal vs informal school construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of dynamic / semi-decade specific estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Report semi-decade-specific estimates of β in dynamic figures, using period-specific coefficients and 90% confidence intervals, with a reference period (1965–69) given district fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display time-varying treatment effects across semi-decades (or other intervals) with reference periods and clustered SEs to illustrate dynamics of schooling entry over time.
